summary: Cast-iron caisson light on a reef in the Taunton River, lit in 1881; keepers, the 1920 rescue, automation in 1963, and private owners since 2010.

structures.note: Caisson sunk on the reef; iron tower and lantern cast elsewhere and shipped July 1881 (LHF). Cost $24,000 (NRHP). Tilted north in 1938 hurricane; a larger caisson later built around it (LHF)
Concrete foundation, about 15 ft of cement (NRHP)

access.note: Privately owned. Tours and overnight stays arranged by the owner (LHF; Herald News via USA TODAY Network, 2024). Shore view from Borden Light Marine at the end of Almond Street.

events.note: $25,000 appropriated on 16 June 1880 after district officers recommended a light (LHF)
Caisson tower built; NRHP gives 1881 and cost $24,000. USLHS: tower established 1881
Lighted for the first time 1 October 1881, fixed red fifth order (LHF)
Fog bell struck by machinery (LHF)
Color changed from red to white (Board report)
Fixed white changed to flashing white, 3 December 1900 per Board narrative (1901 report). Board list gives 31 December
3 August 1912: keeper John H. Paul rescued one of two men from an overturned rowboat; the other drowned. Carnegie medal (LHF)
8 October 1907 gale; barge sank in the harbor, two men drowned, sloop wrecked (keeper's log quoted by LHF)
1 August 1920: keeper John H. Paul rescued two men whose boat capsized (Lighthouse Service Bulletin)
Order changed from fifth to fourth (LHF). USLHS gives the original optic as fourth order: source conflict
Great New England Hurricane tipped the tower a bit to the north; it retains the lean (LHF)
Tower electrified (LHF; USLHS gives electrified 1957 in the LHF narrative)
Station made unattended 17 May 1963 (LHF); USLHS Year Automated 1963
Fresnel lens replaced by a modern optic flashing every 2.5 seconds (LHF; NRHP records a plastic lens in 1977)
Automatic horn replaced the fog bell (LHF)
Light converted to solar power (LHF)
Auctioned by the federal government; winning bidder defaulted on closing (LHF)
Sold to Nick Korstad at auction, bid $56,569, 31 August 2010 (LHF)
Daymark changed: red band painted around the tower (LHF)
Public tours from June 2013; overnight stays shortly after (LHF)
Fog signal deactivated May 2013 (LHF)
Took ownership May 2018 (USA TODAY Network, Herald News); LHF says sold in 2018
Listed for sale at $1,250,000; private sale by the owner (USA TODAY Network, Herald News, November 2024)

corrections.why: The record's 1875 date is not supported by any source read. The NRHP form gives 1881 construction and a $24,000 cost; LighthouseFriends says the cylinder was cast and shipped in July 1881 and lit 1 October 1881; the USLHS record gives tower established 1881.
Same error as the tower's build date. The 1881 built event is already in the record.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1875 date conflicts with the NRHP form, LighthouseFriends and the USLHS record, all of which give 1881. Resolved in favour of 1881 (see corrections).

The Commissioner's commendation text and the Lighthouse Service Bulletin's 1920 text call the station 'Rhode Island' or 'R. I.'. The NRHP form, the Commissioner's own list and the Fall River location all put it in Massachusetts. Story uses Massachusetts.
The Board's 1901 narrative gives 3 December 1900 for the change to flashing white; its list of characteristic changes gives 31 December 1900. Story follows the narrative.

notes_for_editor: 1) Built date: the record's 1875 is wrong on every source read (see corrections). 2) Optic order: the USLHS record says original fourth order; LHF's 1881 notice says fifth order, the Board's 1900 report calls the lamps fifth order, and LHF says the light changed to fourth order in 1932. Not settled. 3) The 1880 purchase date is garbled in the NRHP OCR ('1180'), so it is not used. 4) Focal height: the record has 14.3 m; LHF's 1881 notice says the focal plane is 50 ft above mean low water (about 15.2 m). Not a record field this round. 5) Range: the record has 9.0 nm; the 1881 notice says 12 nautical miles at 15 ft height. Not changed. 6) Covo's end year: archive 1944, LHF 1943; both are given in the story. 7) Sale timing: LHF says the listing was in 2023; USA TODAY Network (Herald News) reports it on 1 November 2024, and a Herald News item of 3 December 2024 is about the same listing (not read in full: 403). No report of a sale after that was found; status in 2026 unconfirmed. 8) The Bulletin text for 1920 is column-jumbled OCR; the quote used sits on one continuous line. The Bulletin's station name is OCR'd and was not quoted. 9) Chronicling America searches for Borden's Flats 1881 returned only unrelated pages. 10) LHF-only claims: the 1880 appropriation, the 1881 notice, the Georgy, Meyer and Paul stories, the Covo daughter's remarks, the 1907 log entry, the 1938 tilt and the 2008-2018 owner sequence. The Globe quotations are footnoted to LHF as the source (the story says 'as LighthouseFriends quotes it'), not to the Boston Globe. 11) Private individuals: the owners named are the publicly operating innkeepers as the sources name them; the Ferias partner is not named. Covo's daughter is not named in the story. Lamplighter Alice O'Neil is named only as the archive roster names her; LHF's unnamed civilian lamplighter is not linked to her. 12) Commissioner scan pages 664 and 391 were confirmed with corpus.py page (the 664 hit is in the commendations; the 391 hit is in a station list). The commendation text is not dated in the OCR, so the story ties the 'Rhode Island' label to the 1 August 1920 rescue on the strength of the matching names, station and rescue wording. 13) Fiscal years: the Board volumes' title pages read 'fiscal year ended June 30, 1900' (scan 74) and 'June 30, 1901' (scans 28, 96). The 1900 colour change is dated only by the year (LHF gives 27 June 1900). 14) The USLHS record says 'Open to Public: Yes' and 'Private Aid: No'; LHF says 'privately owned; tower open for tours and overnight stays'. The story says it is privately owned and open for tours. The access level stays 'private', per the DESIGN.md rule that 'private' applies to a privately owned site. 15) The Herald News has the Sotheby's listing plan, the 2024 prices of the overnight stays, and a ghost story; none is used. 16) The 1938 hurricane tilt is in LHF and in the Herald News (2024); both are footnoted. 17) No photos added (LHF's photos are copyright, Kraig Anderson).
